cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, and his brother Aaron have a message from the LORD, and Israel's elders already believed it. Now these two take it straight to the top: Pharaoh, king of Egypt. No appointment. No small talk. Just walking into the king's court like it's my bakery's front door.

cards.question: Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says.” Why does the LORD want Pharaoh to let His people go?

answers.text: To hold a feast to Him in the wilderness
To go back to their own land for good
To rest from their labor for a season

cards.text: Pharaoh listens to the whole message. Then he fires right back with a question of his own.

cards.question: What does Pharaoh ask Moses and Aaron?

answers.text: Who is the LORD that I should obey Him
Where will your people go after the feast
How many of your people want to leave

cards.question: Pharaoh says he knows the LORD, but he still won't let Israel go.

cards.text: Moses and Aaron try again. The God of the Hebrews has met with us, they say, so please let us go on a three-day journey into the wilderness to sacrifice to the LORD our God. Polite. REAL polite. Like asking your boss for Friday off when you already know how that's gonna go.

cards.question: Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh what the LORD may do if they don't go and sacrifice to Him. What is it?

answers.text: Strike them with plagues or the sword
Send a flood over the whole land
Turn His face away from them

cards.text: Pharaoh wants to know why Moses and Aaron are drawing the people away from their work. Then he snaps, “Get back to your labor!”

cards.question: Pharaoh also says the people of the land are now ___, and Moses and Aaron would be stopping them from their labor.

cards.text: That same day, Pharaoh calls in the taskmasters and the foremen over the people. Oh, he's not just mad. He's SAME-DAY mad.

cards.question: Pharaoh orders that the people will no longer be supplied with ___ for making bricks.

cards.text: From now on, they have to go gather their own straw. That's like telling me I have to GROW my own chocolate chips before every single batch.

cards.question: Since the people now have to gather their own straw, Pharaoh tells the taskmasters to lower the brick quota.
Pharaoh gives the taskmasters a reason the people keep crying out to go and sacrifice to their God. What does he say?

answers.text: Their God is angry with them

cards.question: Pharaoh orders the work made harder so the men will be kept busy and pay no attention to what he calls lies.

cards.text: The taskmasters and foremen go out with Pharaoh's message: no more straw, get your own wherever you can find it, and your workload won't be reduced at all. So the people scatter all over the land of Egypt.

cards.question: The people scatter all over the land of Egypt to gather ___ for straw.

cards.text: And the taskmasters keep pressing them: “Fulfill your quota each day, just as you did when straw was provided.” Friend, that's a boss taking away your laptop and then asking where the report is.

cards.question: The bricks keep coming up short. Who gets beaten for it?

cards.text: The Israelite foremen go straight to Pharaoh: “Why are you treating your servants this way?” No straw, they say, and yet we're still told to make bricks.

cards.question: The foremen tell Pharaoh his servants are being beaten, but the fault is with his own ___.

cards.text: Pharaoh's answer comes out LOUD. He picks one word, and he likes it so much he says it twice.

cards.question: What does Pharaoh call the foremen?

cards.text: SLACKERS! Slackers! And that's why, Pharaoh says, they keep saying, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to the LORD.’

cards.question: Pharaoh tells the foremen they'll get straw again, as long as they still deliver the full quota of bricks.

cards.text: The foremen realize they're in trouble, because the daily quota isn't going down. They walk out from Pharaoh, and who's standing there waiting for them? Moses and Aaron. Oh, this is about to be AWKWARD.

cards.question: What do the foremen say to Moses and Aaron?

answers.text: May the LORD look on you and judge you
Thank you for standing up for us
Go back and ask Pharaoh again

cards.text: They say Moses and Aaron have made them a stench before Pharaoh and his officials. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer under dust and old takeout menus, and NOBODY ever called me a stench.

cards.question: The foremen tell Moses and Aaron they have placed a sword in Pharaoh's hand to kill them.

cards.text: So Moses goes back to the LORD. And he doesn't hold one thing back.

cards.question: Moses comes before the LORD with a question. What does he ask?

answers.text: Why have You brought trouble upon this people
Who will You send to Pharaoh instead of me
How long must Your people wait in Egypt

cards.question: Moses says that ever since he spoke to Pharaoh in the LORD's name, Pharaoh has brought trouble on the people, and the LORD has not ___ His people in any way.

cards.text: Moses brought the hard question. Now the LORD answers him.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Moses he will now see?

answers.text: What the LORD will do to Pharaoh
A new leader rise up in Egypt

cards.question: The LORD says that because of His strong hand, Pharaoh will do something with the people. What is it?

answers.text: Drive them out of his land
Beg them to stay in Egypt
Make them a brand new deal

cards.text: And that's where we'll let this batch cool for now. Trust me, friend, this story is nowhere near done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 2 quotes "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card has five sentences: one long sentence, then 'Now these two take it straight to the top...', 'No appointment.', 'No small talk.' and 'Just walking into the king's court...'. The limit is 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card says Israel's elders already believed the message (Exodus 4:29-31) and that Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). Both facts come from outside the passage, but the card cites only Exodus 5:1, so neither fact carries its reference.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card states that a fact from outside the passage (the elders believing, Exodus 4:31) is true without giving that fact its reference.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The blank 'numerous' tests the exact wording of Exodus 5:5. Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason toward 'numerous' over 'restless' or 'weary', so the right pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'Oh, he's not just mad. He's SAME-DAY mad.' presents Pharaoh's anger as fact. The text never says Pharaoh is angry, and the line doesn't mark the feeling as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: Feelings. He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The blank 'stubble' tests the exact word in Exodus 5:12. The earlier cards give no basis for choosing 'stubble' over 'reeds' or 'grass', so this is a wording guess.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'he likes it so much he says it twice' gives a reason Pharaoh repeats 'Slackers!'. The text never says why he repeats it.

rule.text: Reasons. He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The setup on card 7 ('Oh, this is about to be AWKWARD.') rules out the friendly wrong answer 'Thank you for standing up for us' before the baker answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer 'May the LORD look on you and judge you' sounds like the Bible. The wrong answers 'Thank you for standing up for us' and 'Go back and ask Pharaoh again' sound modern and casual, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Moses' second question in Exodus 5:22, 'Is this why You sent me?', is never told or asked anywhere in the stop. It is a key part of his complaint, so the baker misses it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The story-continues line 'And that's where we'll let this batch cool for now. Trust me, friend, this story is nowhere near done.' copies the doc's example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.') almost word for word instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: The last story card holds only the story-continues line and tells no verse, but it cites Exodus 6:1. The citation rule says a card cites the verses it tells, and this card tells none.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the story-continues line, what should its "verses" field contain: the passage's last verse, the verse of the card before it, or something else?
